note: Official add-ons. RSMPS never bundles or hosts these files: they are fetched from the upstream source below only when the user asks, and are verified against the pinned SHA-256 before anything is run. To update a pin, see docs/RELEASING.md (Add-ons).

addons.name: FFmpeg
addons.title: ProRes-compatible export (via FFmpeg)
addons.description: Encodes video with alpha and professional codecs (ProRes-compatible 422 HQ and 4444, QuickTime Animation, PNG in MOV, WebM with alpha, H.264, H.265). RSMPS does not include FFmpeg; you can download it here or point RSMPS at an FFmpeg you already have.

bringYourOwn.win32: Install FFmpeg yourself (for example: winget install Gyan.FFmpeg) and press Locate, or put ffmpeg.exe on your PATH.
bringYourOwn.darwin: Install FFmpeg yourself (for example: brew install ffmpeg) and press Locate, or put ffmpeg on your PATH.
bringYourOwn.linux: Install FFmpeg with your package manager (for example: sudo apt install ffmpeg) and press Locate, or put ffmpeg on your PATH.

license.name: GPL-3.0-or-later (this build includes GPL libraries such as x264 and x265)

source.name: Gyan Doshi's FFmpeg builds (linked from ffmpeg.org/download.html)

win32-x64.hashSource: SHA-256 published by gyan.dev (ffmpeg-release-essentials.zip.sha256, release 9.0.2). The archive size matches the GitHub asset (114768076 bytes). Recomputed from a download of the URL above on 2026-11-16: the hash and the size match, and the archive contains the three listed files.

addons.name: COLMAP
addons.title: Camera solving for Splat from Video (via COLMAP)
addons.description: Finds where the camera was for every frame of a clip or photo set (structure from motion). Used by the Splat from Video node, together with Brush. Runs on the processor; this build has no NVIDIA acceleration. RSMPS does not include COLMAP.
addons.notice: A large third-party program that runs on your computer (about 230 MB unpacked). The Windows build is not code-signed, so your antivirus may scan or question it the first time it runs.

bringYourOwn.win32: Download COLMAP 4.x for Windows from github.com/colmap/colmap/releases yourself, unpack it and press Locate to pick bin\colmap.exe.
bringYourOwn.darwin: Install COLMAP yourself (for example: brew install colmap) and press Locate to pick the colmap program.
bringYourOwn.linux: COLMAP publishes no Linux download. Install it with your package manager (for example: sudo apt install colmap) or build it, then press Locate to pick the colmap program.

license.name: BSD-3-Clause (COLMAP); the archive also contains third-party libraries under their own licences (for example Qt under LGPL-3.0, Boost, Ceres, OpenImageIO, ONNX Runtime)

source.name: COLMAP releases on GitHub (ETH Zurich and UNC Chapel Hill)

win32-x64.hashSource: SHA-256 shown by GitHub for the release asset (digest field of release 4.2.1). Recomputed from a download of the URL above on 2026-11-16: the hash and the size match. The archive has no LICENSE file: the licence is on the COLMAP website. The archive also holds 148 *_test.exe programs, which are not unpacked.

license.name: BSD-3-Clause (COLMAP); the archive also contains third-party libraries under their own licences

source.name: COLMAP releases on GitHub (ETH Zurich and UNC Chapel Hill)

NOT downloaded or run by the maintainer: the folder layout inside the archive (bin/colmap) is assumed from the Windows build. If the program is not found the install stops with a clear error and nothing is kept.

addons.name: COLMAP (NVIDIA)
addons.title: Faster camera solving on NVIDIA graphics cards (COLMAP with CUDA)
addons.description: The same COLMAP with NVIDIA CUDA acceleration for feature extraction and matching. Only useful with an NVIDIA graphics card; much larger download. When both are installed, Splat from Video uses this one.
addons.notice: A large third-party program that runs on your computer (about 415 MB download). It is not code-signed. It needs an NVIDIA graphics card with a current driver.

bringYourOwn.win32: Install the COLMAP add-on instead, or locate a COLMAP you already have there.
bringYourOwn.darwin: Not available on macOS. Use the COLMAP add-on.
bringYourOwn.linux: Not available here. Use the COLMAP add-on (Locate).

license.name: BSD-3-Clause (COLMAP); the archive also contains third-party libraries under their own licences, including NVIDIA CUDA runtime libraries

source.name: COLMAP releases on GitHub (ETH Zurich and UNC Chapel Hill)

win32-x64.hashSource: SHA-256 shown by GitHub for the release asset (digest field of release 4.2.1); the size is the asset's Content-Length. NOT downloaded or run by the maintainer (the no-CUDA build was tested instead); the layout is assumed to match the no-CUDA build.

addons.name: Brush
addons.title: Gaussian splat training for Splat from Video (via Brush)
addons.description: Trains the Gaussian splats from the frames and the cameras COLMAP found. Runs on your graphics card (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel or Apple). RSMPS does not include Brush.
addons.notice: A large third-party program that runs on your computer and uses your graphics card. The Windows build is not code-signed.

bringYourOwn.darwin: Download Brush 0.3 from github.com/ArthurBrussee/brush/releases yourself and press Locate to pick brush_app.
bringYourOwn.linux: Download Brush 0.3 from github.com/ArthurBrussee/brush/releases yourself and press Locate to pick brush_app.
